body.statement: There exist universal constants \(c_0,c_1,C_1>0\) such that, for every \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), \(M\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}\le c_0\sqrt S\) implies \[c_1\min\{1,\sqrt{S\log(1/\alpha)}\}\le\mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\le C_1\min\{1,\sqrt{S\log(1/\alpha)}\}.\] The infimum defining \(\mathcal R_\alpha\) includes every measurable procedure randomized by \(R\).
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: the confidence-sensitive minimax frontier is characterized over heterogeneous fixed schedules.
body.gap: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012 and RigdonHudgens2015 provide finite two-stage partial-interference intervals for specified binary-effect procedures but no all-procedure expected-length lower bound. The equal-block analysis has one reveal probability and an extreme-confidence cutoff, while KandirosHarshawSavje2026 characterizes mean-squared-error rates with design and estimator as decision variables.
body.consumer: The result supplies a precision benchmark for school, village, and online-network partitions whose component sizes and exposure probabilities vary.
